extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (assistant professor or higher) at U.S. institutions applying to the HHMI Investigator program; mid-career faculty seeking HHMI funding
extracted.subtask_description: Selection and eligibility criteria for the Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) Investigator program, describing who may apply and the attributes HHMI seeks (people-focused, mid-career researchers committed primarily to research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection philosophy: people, not projects
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI is guided by the principle of "people, not projects" when selecting Investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI expects to support talented, productive scientists rather than specific projects; selection focuses on the individual’s attributes and potential rather than project-based proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should be "talented and productive scientists who demonstrate a combination of specific attributes that clearly distinguish them from other highly competent researchers in the field."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI looks for candidates who stand out relative to peers by a combination of attributes (see evaluation approach items such as originality, leadership, independent thinking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold a PhD and/or MD (or the equivalent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic appointment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a tenured or tenure-track position as an assistant professor or higher academic rank (or the equivalent) at an eligible U.S. institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment must be at an eligible U.S. institution and at the stated ranks (assistant professor or higher) or formal equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-training experience window
rubrics_metrics.description: Have more than five, but no more than 15, years of post-training, professional experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must fall within this post-training experience range to be eligible (i.e., >5 and ≤15 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Active PI on qualifying grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Be the principal investigator on one or more active, national peer-reviewed research grants with an initial duration of at least three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualifying support must be national peer-reviewed research grants with initial duration ≥3 years. Mentored awards and training grants do not qualify. Multi-investigator grants may qualify (i.e., having a PI role on such grants can meet this requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentored/training awards exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentored awards and training grants do not qualify as the required active, national peer-reviewed research grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant’s only support is mentored or training grants, they do not meet the grant-PI eligibility requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research time commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must plan to dedicate at least 75% of their time to research in an eligible discipline at an eligible U.S. institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI expects Investigators to spend the majority of their professional effort on research (≥75%); this must be at an eligible U.S. institution and in an eligible discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible research disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI invites researchers who bring original and innovative approaches to the investigation of biological problems in: biomedical disciplines; plant biology; evolutionary biology; biophysics; chemical biology; biomedical engineering; computational biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should work in one of these listed disciplines and propose original, innovative approaches to biological problems. The list defines the program’s eligible topical scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and creativity over conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI emphasizes originality and creativity over conformity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors novel, creative approaches rather than work that conforms to prevailing fashions or incremental extensions of others’ work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to take risks / preliminary-data-independent work
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI emphasizes risk-taking research that may not yet have preliminary data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI is open to supporting high-risk, high-reward research; lack of preliminary data is not necessarily a disqualifier if the idea is compelling and innovative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record of independent thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI emphasizes a track record of independent thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate intellectual independence in their past work—evidence that they initiate and lead original lines of inquiry rather than primarily continuing mentors’ projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated leadership in the field
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI emphasizes demonstrated leadership in their field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership may be shown through leading labs, shaping research directions, mentoring others, organizing scientific efforts, or other evidence of influence in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for long-term paradigm-shifting research
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI emphasizes potential for paradigm-shifting research over the long term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection prioritizes candidates whose work has the potential to change how problems are approached in their field over an extended timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research assessment per DORA (avoid journal impact factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI signed DORA, committing to assess research on its own merits rather than relying on journal impact factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation will focus on the substance and merit of the research outputs themselves (e.g., quality, originality, significance) rather than proxies such as journal impact factors.
